what: selector research at WingtraCloud 84d3721b (read, then checked)

checked.fact: I re-read every cited line at commit 84d3721b33ee195738a2a002313c55becb2643bc (git describe 1.74.0-6-g84d3721b3), offline (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1). Every blob I needed was local. Most citations were right. The corrections below are marked 'Corrected:' and new controls are marked 'New:'.

checked.topic: Button testid mechanics (applies to all items)
checked.fact: The shared Button takes the prop `testid`, which defaults to 'none'. It renders <button data-testid="btn-wrapper-<testid>"> around an inner <span data-testid="<testid>">. So every untagged Button shows up as btn-wrapper-none / none, which is not unique, and has to be matched by exact visible text. ButtonProps has no aria-label prop, so none of the write-list Buttons has an aria-label.
checked.selector: testid:<id> matches the inner span; testid:btn-wrapper-<id> matches the <button>

checked.fact: The optional native-update prompt has the title 'Update WingtraApp on this tablet?' (updates.do_you_want_to_install_the_update) and the description 'After confirmation you will be asked to install the new version of the app'. It is built with getConfirmation(action=updates.update_now, cancel=general.not_now) and rendered by the global AsyncModal into ConfirmDialog. config.id is not set, and ConfirmDialog passes id only to Dialog.Content, so the panel gets floating-ui's generated id. aria-labelledby points at the Dialog.Header div.

Label 'Update now' (updates.update_now). It is the ConfirmDialog action Button with testid 'btn-dialog-action': inner span btn-dialog-action, button btn-wrapper-btn-dialog-action. The handler is on onMouseDown (with preventDefault), not onClick. A real tap fires it, because the WebView emits mousedown after a tap. JS element.click() does not fire it. On confirm, if the drone is not armed, it calls UpdaterPlugin.installApk. btn-dialog-action is shared: 21 non-test files call getConfirmation( and 6 render <ConfirmDialog> directly, so scope the selector by the dialog title. Corrected: the first pass said 'any touch-down triggers it' and gave a count of 27 files. The same text 'Update now' is also used by the OTA and SD-card firmware dialogs (updates.firmware_update.start_update_cta).
checked.selector: text:Update now inside the dialog titled 'Update WingtraApp on this tablet?' (testid btn-dialog-action is shared)

checked.fact: Label 'Not now' (general.not_now). It is the ConfirmDialog cancel Button with no testid (btn-wrapper-none / none). It postpones the install and logs 'the user postponed it'. general.not_now is also used by the bundle-restart dialog and the OTA firmware confirm dialog.

When isUpdateRequired(APP_VERSION, latestBuild.version_name) is true, the prompt has the title 'To continue using the app install the latest version' and one 'Install' button (updates.install). It has hideClose, hideCancel and dismissDisabled set, and keepOpenOnConfirm keeps it open after confirm. onConfirmed calls UpdaterPlugin.installApk unless the drone is armed. The button is the shared btn-dialog-action. updates.install is used only here. Match it as an exact string, because other en.json strings contain 'Install', for example 'Install new propellers' and the help text 'Install WingtraCloud on your OS...'.
checked.selector: exact text:Install inside the dialog titled 'To continue using the app install the latest version'

checked.topic: 2 Install: Android system screens after confirm
checked.fact: UpdaterPlugin.installApk first checks canRequestPackageInstalls(). If that is false, it opens Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES (the 'Install unknown apps' screen) and returns. Otherwise it starts Intent.ACTION_VIEW with type application/vnd.android.package-archive, which opens Android's package installer with its own Install/Update button. Both screens are native, outside the WebView. CDP cannot see them, and an adb tap helper must not press anything on them. Corrected: added the unknown-sources branch.
checked.selector: native UI: 'Install unknown apps' settings and the system package installer

checked.fact: The native Compose screen shown when the system WebView is too old has two buttons: 'Update from GooglePlay' (onDownloadFromGooglePlayClick) and 'Download update files' (onDownloadFromApkClick). Both are native and have no testTag.
checked.selector: text:Update from GooglePlay / text:Download update files (native)

checked.fact: After a new web bundle downloads, the dialog 'Restart Wingtra app to update' offers 'Restart now' (updates.restart_now) and 'Not now'. Restart now calls LiveUpdate.reload(), which applies the bundle. In the forced variant (isRestartRequired), close and Not now are hidden, dismiss is disabled, and reload runs in onConfirmed. The dialog appears only when notifyUser or isRestartRequired is true. Automatic checks otherwise show only a 'Downloaded update...' toast. The action is the shared btn-dialog-action.
checked.selector: text:Restart now inside the dialog titled 'Restart Wingtra app to update'

checked.topic: 1 Check for updates (Settings > About, Fleet drone)
checked.fact: Label 'Check for updates' (updates.check_for_updates). It is an outlined Button with no testid (btn-wrapper-none). It appears on Settings > About on Android only (notifyUser, fleetCheck). It also appears in the Fleet drone FirmwareInfo panel (notifyUser, droneCodesToCheck=[droneCode]) unless the drone status is inactive. When online, performUpdateCheck shows the 'Update checks are currently unavailable' toast and returns unless isAndroid && AutoUpdate flag && PROD. Otherwise it downloads an APK if one exists, then checks the bundle and firmware, which can open the APK, restart or OTA dialogs. Corrected: when offline on Android, checkUpdate runs checkFirmwareUpdate directly through execOfflineCompatibleFn and skips that gate, so cached firmware can still open the OTA dialog.

checked.topic: New: update dialogs can open without any tap
checked.fact: Automatic checks call checkUpdate with notifyUser:false at four points: (1) at startup through useAppUpdate, unless a flight is being continued; (2) through useScheduledAppUpdateCheck, at most once a day; (3) when a drone first connects, through useDroneConnects; (4) after drone activation. A downloaded APK is always prompted through promptNativeUpdate, regardless of notifyUser. A firmware update for the connected drone opens the 'Update drone firmware?' OTA modal even when notifyUser is false. The SD-card 'Update drone firmware?' dialog opens when the drone's OBC reports OBC_ASK_UPDATE. A tap-automation guard therefore has to check for these dialogs before every tap, not only after a tap on 'Check for updates'.
checked.selector: [data-modal-overlay] [role="dialog"] whose title is one of the update titles

checked.fact: The visible text is 'Start mocklink', hardcoded with a lowercase m. It is an outlined Button with testid 'btn-start-mocklink', and onClick calls WiPPlugin.startMocklink with the page's options. The page is the tab with testid 'plane-tab-mocklink' (title 'Mocklink'). The MOCKLINK flag hides only the tab button: /plane/mocklink is always routed.

The visible text is 'Stop mocklink' (hardcoded). It is an outlined Button with testid 'btn-stop-mocklink', disabled unless activeVehicleAvailable && activeLinkIsMocklink. onClick calls WiPPlugin.stopMocklink(). A case-insensitive text match also hits the Swiss-knife 'Stop Mocklink' button, so use the testid.

checked.topic: 3 MockLink controls in the Swiss Army Knife popup
checked.fact: The 'Dev help tools' popup has 'Start default Mocklink' (WiPPlugin.startMocklink with defaults built from the last valid payload) and 'Stop Mocklink' (WiPPlugin.stopMocklink, disabled unless the active link is MockLink). Neither has a testid. Both show only when isAndroid && DEV_FLYING && MOCKLINK. New: when the ShowTelemetryDropInSwissKnife flag is also on, the popup has a 'Package drop percentage' slider (name packageDropPercentageSlider). Each change calls WiPPlugin.setPackageDropPercentage, which alters link behaviour.
checked.selector: text:Start default Mocklink / exact text:Stop Mocklink / input[name="packageDropPercentageSlider"]

checked.fact: Hardcoded label 'Update connected drone'. It is an outlined Button with no testid, and onClick runs startDebugOtaUpdate. It is disabled unless connectedVehicleIp is set and no debug update is in progress. There is no confirmation dialog: the handler picks the newest compatible release (or the older debug tag when the 'Downgrade' toggle, testId debug-ota-use-older-firmware, is on) and calls performHttpUpdate straight away. The tab testid is 'plane-tab-ota-debug' (title 'OTA Debug'). It sits behind the MOCKLINK tab flag, but the route is always registered.

checked.topic: 4 OTA Debug network controls (adjacent write actions)
checked.fact: The same page has three hardcoded buttons without testids: 'Establish OTA connection' (WiPPlugin.startOtaConnection, needs an active vehicle), 'Create OTA network' (WiPPlugin.createDebugOtaNetwork) and 'Close OTA network' (WiPPlugin.closeDebugOtaNetwork). They change the drone and tablet OTA Wi-Fi state. Once a network exists, the page shows its passphrase in data-testid debug-ota-network-passphrase, so do not dump that text into logs.
checked.selector: text:Establish OTA connection / text:Create OTA network / text:Close OTA network

checked.fact: The dialog title is 'Update drone firmware?' (updates.firmware_update.ask_update). The 'Update now' Button (start_update_cta) has testid 'ota-update-now'. If the OTADroneUpdates flag is on and OTA is supported, onConfirm is startOtaUpdate. That runs the pre-update checks (which can route to the battery-too-low or turn-off-Wi-Fi modals), then WiPPlugin.startOtaConnection(). Once the drone IP arrives, the HTTP firmware upload starts on its own. If the flag is off or OTA is unsupported, the button switches to the SD-card workflow instead. OtaUpdateModal renders this dialog in the AskUpdate state and is mounted globally on Android. The container is dismissDisabled.

The 'Not now' Button (general.not_now) has testid 'ota-update-not-now'. onClose runs endOtaUpdateWorkflow, and the button is disabled while a start is pending. The repo's own E2E dismisses it with [data-testid="btn-wrapper-ota-update-not-now"]. Below the actions is the link 'Having issues? Update via SD card', an ExternalLinkButton with no testid that calls switchToSdCardWorkflow (it opens the copy-to-SD modal and does not write by itself).

In the TurnOffWifi state, the 'Continue' Button (actions.continue) has testid 'ota-wifi-off-continue' but no onClick of its own. The click handler continueOtaUpdate sits on the wrapper div data-testid 'ota-wifi-off-continue-wrapper'. It shows a 'Turn off Wi-Fi before continuing.' toast while Wi-Fi is on, and otherwise calls onContinue = startOtaUpdate, which starts the firmware update. Corrected: the first pass did not say that the handler is on the wrapper div. The neighbouring 'Open Wi-Fi settings' button has testid ota-open-wifi-panel.

In the BatteryTooLow state, the modal (data-testid ota-tablet-battery-too-low-modal) has 'Close' (testid ota-battery-too-low-close) and 'Update via SD card' (testid ota-battery-too-low-sd-card). The second calls switchToSdCardWorkflow, which leads to the 'Copy to SD card' write but does not write by itself.

The dialog title is 'Update drone firmware?' (updates.sd_card_update.ask_update), with the description 'Updating takes up to 7 minutes. Connection to the drone will be lost during the update.'. Its only button is 'Update now' (updates.firmware_update.start_update_cta), with no testid. In AskUpdate, close is hidden and dismiss is disabled, so the dialog has no decline control. The handler calls WiPPlugin.setObcUpdateInProgress and sendOBCUpdateAck(DO_UPDATE). The dialog opens on its own when the OBC reports OBC_ASK_UPDATE. If the OBC asks again while the update is InProgress, DO_UPDATE is re-sent without a tap. SdCardUpdateModal is mounted globally on Android.
checked.selector: text:Update now inside the dialog whose description starts 'Updating takes up to 7 minutes'

checked.fact: The 'Copy to SD card' Button (updates.sd_card_update.copy_to_sd_card_cta) has no testid and is shown in the SelectFolder and Error states. handleCopy calls copyFirmwareUpdateToPickedFolder, which writes the firmware file to the folder the user picks.

Corrected: 'Update WO' and 'Update WR' are table column headers. The buttons under them are icon-only Buttons (ExportProjectIcon) with no text and no testid, each wrapped in a div with data-testid 'firmware-update-action'. That wrapper repeats on every row and in both columns. startUpdate opens the OtaUpdate modal and navigates to '/', and the real gate is then ota-update-now. The Download column's icon Button (DownloadIcon, no testid) calls ensureFirmwareReleaseDownloaded, which writes the firmware to the tablet. 'Refresh available updates' is read-only. The tab testid is plane-tab-plane-updates.

checked.fact: An icon-only filled Button (SwissKnife icon, teal) sits in a div at absolute top-0 left-0. It has no text, testid (btn-wrapper-none) or aria-label, and opens the 'Dev help tools' popup. It renders only with the DevReporting flag. The popup is a plain div with an <h2>, not a role=dialog. Its close X is a div data-testid 'btn-close-modal', the same testid the Dialog close uses.

checked.fact: Hardcoded label 'Report bug', an orange Button with no testid. It only opens ReportingModal and writes nothing by itself.

The 'Next' text is hardcoded. It is a Button type=submit form={formId} with no testid (btn-wrapper-none), in the dialog headed 'Report'. The title is pre-filled with '[CT] <date>' and the description with the template, so the form is valid as soon as it opens. Submit runs onSubmit. That shares the last valid flight as ANYONE_WITH_LINK with file export (a cloud sharing write), calls clickupProxyApi.createTask, sets custom fields (reporter, platform, env, version, build time) and starts log auto-attachment. The toggle label 'Attach more files in the next step' contains 'next', so match 'Next' exactly. Corrected: the share citation is now 195-208.

checked.fact: Title (name=title) and Tablet name (name=tabletName) are single-line inputs inside <form id={formId}>, and the submit button is linked through its form attribute. TextField's onKeyDown only filters +, - and e for number inputs, so Enter is not blocked. Standard HTML implicit submission therefore means an Enter or newline typed into those inputs submits the report, just as 'Next' does. This is inferred from the code and not tested on a device. The Description textarea does not submit on Enter.

The done step has 'Go to ticket' (window.open of app.clickup.com/t/<id>) and 'Finish' (handleClose). Neither has a testid. The in-progress and done containers both use data-testid 'flight-success-modal-pop-up'.

checked.topic: 1. About label: how it is built
checked.fact: The Settings > About badge, titled 'WingtraCloud version', shows versionLabel. That is `${APP_VERSION}-${APP_ENVIRONMENT}` in production and `${APP_VERSION}-${APP_ENVIRONMENT}-${GIT_HASH_SHORT}` otherwise. The Badge has no testid.

APP_VERSION is a Vite define, JSON.stringify(process.env.npm_package_version), which is the apps/package.json version (1.74.0 at this ref). It is declared only as an ambient const and inlined into the bundle, so it is not a window property.
GIT_HASH is `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` at build time, and GIT_HASH_SHORT is hash.slice(0,7). Both are Vite defines inlined at build. No global, meta tag or localStorage key holds them.

checked.topic: 1. Hash reachable only through the bundle text (inference, check on device)
checked.fact: ReportingModal builds 'App info': { Version: APP_VERSION, Environment: APP_ENVIRONMENT, ..., 'Git hash': GIT_HASH }. It is statically imported along this chain: DevHelpTools:19, AppLayout:6, ProtectedRoute:24, App:13, LoadingApp:2, index.tsx:26. vite.config sets no manualChunks, so the 40-character literal should be in the eagerly loaded entry chunk. Fetching that same-origin script is a read-only GET. The minified key spacing is assumed and not checked against a real build.
checked.selector: Runtime.evaluate awaitPromise:true: (async()=>{const s=document.querySelector('script[type="module"][src]');const t=await (await fetch(s.src)).text();const h=(t.match(/"Git hash":\s*"([0-9a-f]{40})"/)||[])[1];const v=(t.match(/"App info":\s*\{\s*Version:\s*"([^"]+)"/)||[])[1];return {entry:s.src.split('/').pop(),version:v,gitHash:h,hash7:h&&h.slice(0,7)};})()

checked.fact: On Android, About shows 'WingtraCloud native layer version' from LiveUpdate.getVersionCode(), which returns {versionCode}. The plugin is registered as LiveUpdate (@capawesome/capacitor-live-update 8.6.0). The call is read-only.

checked.topic: 1. LiveUpdate.getCurrentBundle does not give the hash
checked.fact: getCurrentBundle() returns {bundleId}. The APK's embedded bundle has no bundleId (code comment). CI uploads bundles with only appId, token, channel, path and androidMin/Max/Eq: no git hash. bundleId says only whether a live bundle is active.

checked.topic: 1. Other places that show the version without opening About
checked.fact: Plane > System overview shows 'WingtraCloud version' followed by `${APP_VERSION}-${APP_ENVIRONMENT}. ${BUILD_TIME_FORMATTED}`, with no hash. The mobile drawer shows 'Cloud version: ' + APP_VERSION. useMetadataLogging sends `${APP_VERSION}-${GIT_HASH_SHORT}` and APP_ENVIRONMENT to native through WiPPlugin.updateMetadataUserProperty. That call is a setter only.

checked.topic: 1. Sentry client carries release = APP_VERSION (Sentry internals, unverified)
checked.fact: Both SentryCapacitor.init and SentryReact.init get release: APP_VERSION, environment: VITE_SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT (CI: inputs.environment) and enabled: PROD. @sentry/react is 8.42.0. Reading this relies on the window.__SENTRY__ carrier internals and gives the version without the hash. The expression returns only release, environment and enabled, never the DSN.
localStorageItems.ts has no key matching version, environment or hash. The Unleash context carries platform and swVersion: APP_VERSION as module config, not a window global.

APP_ENVIRONMENT ('develop'|'staging'|'preproduction'|'production') is import.meta.env.VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT, baked in at build. CI sets it from inputs.environment: sky-production gives production, sky-preproduction gives preproduction, sky-staging gives staging, and any other branch gives develop.
checked.selector: not a global by this name

checked.fact: index.html sets window.env = { VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT: '<%= VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT %>' }, filled by createHtmlPlugin at build. It is part of the web bundle, so it reflects the live bundle in use. It also gates Heap, which loads only in production.

checked.topic: 2. Entry script filename carries the environment
checked.fact: The entry and chunk names are `[name]-[hash]-${ENV}.js` with ENV = VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT. [hash] is a content hash, not the git hash.

checked.topic: 2. E2E globals only on develop/staging Android
checked.fact: window.__wingtraE2EApiRequest and window.__wingtraE2EDownloadMapTiles are registered only on Android when APP_ENVIRONMENT is develop or staging. They are a secondary env signal. Do not call them.

On Android the origin is https://${CAPACITOR_HOSTNAME}. It is http when the hostname is 'localhost', and APP_URL when USE_SERVER=true. .env.common sets localhost and USE_SERVER=true for local dev. CI sets CAPACITOR_HOSTNAME from a GitHub variable whose values are not in the repo. Corrected: platform is 'electron' when window.electron exists, and otherwise Capacitor.getPlatform().

checked.topic: 2. API base is baked, not global
checked.fact: WINGTRA_API_URI is resolveWingtraApiUrl(VITE_APP_WINGTRA_API_URI || 'http://localhost:9016'), with CI setting vars.API_URL. It is a module constant only.

The app uses createBrowserRouter with '*' mapped to LoadingApp, so location.pathname is the route. Under '/': the index and unknown paths redirect to /sites; the other routes are /sites/create, /sites/:siteId/*, /flights/:flightId?, /maps/*, /settings/*, /plane/*, /fleet/:droneId?/*, /help/*, /history/*, /processing/*, /object-detection/*, /survey-outcomes and /detect-anything. /log-analysis and /telemetry-analysis exist only with the LogAnalysisTool flag. Public routes start with /shared.

Under /sites/:siteId: site-details, flights?/* (the site tabs; the 'flights' segment is optional), planning/:flightId, fly/:flightId and surveying/:flightId. Anything else redirects to flights. The site tabs are flights-overview/:flightId? and maps/:datasetId?, and unknown tabs show a 404 stub. Corrected: urls.ts builds only the flights-tab link, /sites/:siteId/flights/flights-overview/:flightId?. The maps tab path is defined in SiteTabsLayout and routes to /sites/:siteId/flights/maps/:datasetId?.
The flights table is /flights, and a focused flight is /flights/:flightId.

The maps table is /maps/:datasetId?. The viewer is /maps/:datasetId/map-viewer/:viewerId/*. /maps/:datasetId/overview/* holds export/* (files and processing-history; anything else redirects to files) and legacy-viewer. ExportRoutesEnum.Reports has no route.

/plane redirects to system-overview. The tabs are system-overview, mocklink, debug, ota-debug, plane-updates, plane-parameters, telemetry-settings-debug (title 'Telemetry Tools', testid plane-tab-telemetry-dev-tools), metadata-upload and powersync. The Mocklink flag shows the mocklink, debug and ota-debug tabs, MetadataDebugPage shows metadata-upload, and OfflineSync shows powersync. The flags hide only the tab buttons: every route is registered.
/settings redirects to account. The sub-routes are account, organization, users, global, flights, processing, about and subscriptions/:seePlans?. SettingsEnum.UsageData has no route.
Fleet is /fleet, and /fleet/:droneId opens the drone sidebar. Closing the sidebar navigates to /fleet with replace. Help is /help/*.

There are 1249 non-test .tsx files. In non-test tsx, ' testid=' gives 178 lines in 122 files and ' testId=' gives 157 lines in 90 files. Other hooks: aria-label= 46 hits in 40 files, role= 23 in 21, static id="..." 21 in 18. Corrected: name="..." gives 182 hits in 67 files, not 184 in 69. checked.fact: The prop is `testid` (lowercase), default 'none'. The <button> gets data-testid="btn-wrapper-<testid>" and type={type}. The inner span gets data-testid="<testid>", and the loading spinner gets spinner-for-<testid>. Tap the <button> wrapper, not the span.

The prop is `testId` (camelCase), and data-testid is forbidden at the type level. The <button> gets data-testid={testId}, which is undefined when unset. There is no default aria-label and no explicit type.

TextField takes `testId` and puts data-testid on the <input>. The input id comes from useId(), so it is unstable. restProps, including name=, are spread onto the input after id. FormTextField always passes name, so every react-hook-form text field has input[name="<field>"].

checked.topic: 1 other shared components that emit data-testid
checked.fact: These take lowercase `testid`: Checkbox (plus data-testparam), Typography, Badge, Spinner, SwipeToConfirm, PageNavbar, AppTabs Tab (config.testid). Most modals use the in-house Dialog: Dialog.Container 109 hits in 105 files, Dialog.Content 125 in 120, Dialog.Header 93 in 89. Corrected: the only third-party modal is flowbite-react Modal, imported in ObjectDetection FullImageView.jsx (not on the write list); no material-tailwind Dialog is imported. The source never writes role="dialog". The role comes from floating-ui useRole (default 'dialog') spread through getFloatingProps; that is library behaviour, so confirm it on the device. The panel gets aria-labelledby from Dialog.Header (a div) and aria-describedby from Dialog.Description. Its id is props.id ?? the Container id ?? floating-ui's id. className is set after the spread, so ConfirmDialog's className 'Dialog' never reaches the DOM. The panel is portaled into #router-outlet inside FloatingOverlay [data-modal-overlay]. Content mounts only while open. Escape and an outside pointerdown dismiss it unless dismissDisabled.

The X is a <div data-testid="btn-close-modal"> holding an IconButton <button> with no testid, no aria-label and tabIndex -1. It is not rendered with hideClose. Dialog.Close (4 files) is a Button with testid btn-close-modal, rendering btn-wrapper-btn-close-modal plus the span. New: the Swiss-knife popup's close X is also a div data-testid btn-close-modal, outside any dialog. Bare [data-testid="btn-close-modal"] is therefore ambiguous.

The global AsyncModal renders ConfirmDialog. The cancel Button has no testid (btn-wrapper-none). The action Button has testid btn-dialog-action and fires on onMouseDown with preventDefault and stopPropagation. An adb tap works; element.click() does not, so dispatch mousedown instead.

/login has FormTextFields name="email" and name="password" (type password, which switches to text when the eye icon is tapped). Neither has a testId. The Login button is an orange Button type=submit form={formId} with the text 'Login' and no testid. The <h1> also reads 'Login'. A GraphQL 404 shows an error under the email field and a 403 under the password field. A connection error and other errors show toasts. Links: forgot-password-btn and create-new-account-btn. The E2E LoginPage uses the same selectors.

The app uses react-toastify 9.1.3. One ToastContainer is set to bottom-right with hideProgressBar, icon={false} and closeButton={false}. toastr.css overrides the stock .Toastify__toast-container, __toast, __toast-body and __toast--default, --info, --success, --warning and --error classes. ToastType values are success, warning, info and error. FlyToastr reuses the same container.

Each toast's content is a div data-testid 'notification-label' holding a title (default 'Unexpected error' when an error is passed) and the text. Its close button has aria-label 'Close' and data-testid 'notification-close'. Auto-close times: success 5000 ms, warning 10000 ms, neutral (info) 5000 ms, error 10000 ms. FlyToastr's BlockingError never auto-closes.

'Report sent' is Typography text in ReportingModal's done state, inside div data-testid flight-success-modal-pop-up, followed by 'Go to ticket' and 'Finish' (both untagged). The in-progress state 'Reporting ...' reuses the same testid, and while it is shown the X is hidden and dismiss is disabled. ReportingModal's real toasts are: the warning "Couldn't attach the flight plan link..."; the error "Couldn't create report, retry or cancel."; 'ClickUp task not created yet.'; 'Failed to auto attach log files.'; and 'Failed to upload one or more files.'.

first_pass.topic: 1. About label: how it is built
first_pass.fact: The Settings > About badge (title 'WingtraCloud version') is versionLabel = APP_ENVIRONMENT === 'production' ? `${APP_VERSION}-${APP_ENVIRONMENT}` : `${APP_VERSION}-${APP_ENVIRONMENT}-${GIT_HASH_SHORT}`. Production has no hash. The Badge gets no testid, so after navigating it can only be found by its text.

APP_VERSION is a Vite compile-time `define` = JSON.stringify(process.env.npm_package_version), which is the apps/package.json version (1.74.0 at this ref). It is declared only as an ambient TS const. It is not a window property; the literal is inlined into the bundle.
first_pass.selector: none as a global (typeof APP_VERSION === 'undefined' in page scope)

first_pass.fact: GIT_HASH = `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` of the repo at build time. GIT_HASH_SHORT = hash.slice(0,7), a fixed 7 characters. Both are Vite `define` constants inlined at build and declared as ambient consts. No window global, meta tag or localStorage key holds them.

first_pass.topic: 1. Hash reachable only through the bundle text (inference, check on device)
first_pass.fact: ReportingModal builds an object with 'App info': { Version: APP_VERSION, Environment: APP_ENVIRONMENT, ..., 'Git hash': GIT_HASH }. ReportingModal is statically imported through DevHelpTools <- AppLayout <- ProtectedRoute <- App <- LoadingApp <- index.tsx. vite.config sets no manualChunks, so the full 40-char hash literal should be in the eagerly loaded entry chunk. Fetching that same-origin script and running a regex is a read-only GET. Not run against a real build: the minified key spacing is assumed.
first_pass.selector: Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise:true: (async()=>{const s=document.querySelector('script[type="module"][src]');const t=await (await fetch(s.src)).text();const h=(t.match(/"Git hash":\s*"([0-9a-f]{40})"/)||[])[1];const v=(t.match(/"App info":\s*\{\s*Version:\s*"([^"]+)"/)||[])[1];return {entry:s.src.split('/').pop(),version:v,gitHash:h,hash7:h&&h.slice(0,7)};})()

first_pass.fact: About shows 'WingtraCloud native layer version' from LiveUpdate.getVersionCode() (Android only); the result is {versionCode: string}. The plugin is registered as LiveUpdate (@capawesome/capacitor-live-update 8.6.0). The call is read-only and reachable from page JS through the Capacitor bridge.

first_pass.topic: 1. LiveUpdate.getCurrentBundle does not give the hash
first_pass.fact: getCurrentBundle() returns {bundleId}. The bundleId is Capawesome's own ID, and it is null for the bundle embedded in the APK (code comment). CI uploads the bundle with appId/channel/path/androidMin/Max/Eq only, with no git hash or name. The app logs 'Checking for app updates. Current bundle ID: ...'. The bundleId tells you whether a live bundle is active, not which commit it is.

first_pass.topic: 1. Other places that show the version without opening About
first_pass.fact: Plane > System overview shows `${APP_VERSION}-${APP_ENVIRONMENT}. ${BUILD_TIME_FORMATTED}`, with no hash. The navbar drawer shows 'Cloud version: ' + APP_VERSION. useMetadataLogging sends `${APP_VERSION}-${GIT_HASH_SHORT}` and APP_ENVIRONMENT to native through WiPPlugin.updateMetadataUserProperty (setter only; JS does not read it back here).

first_pass.topic: 1. Sentry client carries release = APP_VERSION (Sentry internals, unverified)
first_pass.fact: Sentry is initialised with release: APP_VERSION and environment: VITE_SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT (CI sets it to the same inputs.environment). @sentry/react is 8.42.0. Reading it relies on the window.__SENTRY__ carrier internals, not on repo code, and gives the version without the hash. The expression returns only release/environment/enabled and never the DSN.
localStorageItems.ts has no version, environment or hash key (grep empty). The Unleash context carries swVersion: APP_VERSION and platform, but the client is a module object, not a window global.

APP_ENVIRONMENT: 'develop'|'staging'|'preproduction'|'production' = import.meta.env.VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT, baked at build. CI sets VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT = inputs.environment from setup.yaml: sky-production->production, sky-preproduction->preproduction, sky-staging->staging, anything else (sky and feature/_build_apk branches) -> develop.
first_pass.selector: not a global by this name

first_pass.fact: index.html runs an inline script `window.env = { VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT: '<%= VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT %>' }`, filled at build by vite-plugin-html createHtmlPlugin from process.env.VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT. It is part of the web bundle, so after a live update it describes the bundle in use. It also gates Heap (loaded only in production).

first_pass.topic: 2. Entry script filename carries the environment
first_pass.fact: Rollup output names are `[name]-[hash]-${ENV}.js` with ENV = VITE_APP_ENVIRONMENT, for entry and chunks. The env can be read from the loaded script URL. The [hash] here is a content hash, not the git hash.

first_pass.topic: 2. E2E globals only on develop/staging Android
first_pass.fact: index.tsx registers window.__wingtraE2EApiRequest and window.__wingtraE2EDownloadMapTiles only when APP_ENVIRONMENT is develop or staging and the platform is Android. Their presence is a secondary env signal; do not call them.

On Android the WebView origin is https://${CAPACITOR_HOSTNAME}. It is http when the hostname is localhost (local dev default in .env.common), or APP_URL when USE_SERVER=true. CAPACITOR_HOSTNAME is a GitHub variable whose per-env values are not in the repo, and it is baked into the APK's native config, not the live bundle, so window.env is the more direct read. Platform comes from Capacitor.getPlatform() ('android'|'web'|'electron').

first_pass.topic: 2. API base is baked, not global
first_pass.fact: WINGTRA_API_URI = import.meta.env.VITE_APP_WINGTRA_API_URI (CI: vars.API_URL), or http://localhost:9016, or a devcontainer override. It is a module constant only, with no window property.

Protected routes under '/': /sites (default; index and unknown paths redirect there), /sites/create, /sites/:siteId/*, /flights/:flightId?, /maps/*, /settings/*, /plane/*, /fleet/:droneId?/*, /help/*, /history/*, /processing/*, /object-detection/*, /detect-anything, /survey-outcomes. /log-analysis and /telemetry-analysis exist only when flag LogAnalysisTool is on. Public share routes start with /shared.

Under /sites/:siteId: site-details, flights?/* (site tabs), planning/:flightId, fly/:flightId, surveying/:flightId; anything else redirects to flights. Site tabs: flights-overview/:flightId? and maps/:datasetId?. The app builds links as /sites/:siteId/flights/flights-overview/:flightId? and /sites/:siteId/flights/maps/:datasetId?. Unknown tab paths show a 404 stub.
The flights table is /flights; a focused flight is /flights/:flightId.

Maps: /maps/:datasetId? is the table; /maps/:datasetId/map-viewer/:viewerId/* is the viewer; /maps/:datasetId/overview/* holds export/* (files, processing-history; anything else redirects to files) and legacy-viewer. ExportRoutesEnum.Reports exists but has no route.

first_pass.fact: The Button prop is `testid` (lowercase) and defaults to 'none'. The <button> element (material-tailwind) gets data-testid="btn-wrapper-<testid>" and type={type}. The inner span gets data-testid="<testid>". The loading spinner gets testid spinner-for-<testid>. So every untagged Button renders data-testid="btn-wrapper-none" and "none", which is useless and not unique. To tap, target the wrapper on the <button>, not the span.

The IconButton prop is `testId` (camelCase). Passing data-testid directly is forbidden at the type level. The <button> gets data-testid={testId}, which is undefined when unset. There is no default aria-label.

TextField takes `testId` and puts data-testid on the <input>. The input id is React useId(), so it is unstable (e.g. ':r3:') and not usable. The label uses htmlFor that unstable id. restProps, including name=, are spread onto the <input> after id, so name= is stable. FormTextField always passes name={name} to TextField, so every react-hook-form text field has input[name="<field>"].

AI is not a link. AiToolsButton renders <button type="button"> with MagicIcon and Typography text t('navbar.ai_tools') = 'AI'. It has no testid and no href, and clicking it opens AiToolsDialog (it does not navigate). It is rendered only when Unleash flag DetectAnything is on. It shows as active when the dialog is open or the path is /detect-anything.
first_pass.selector: button[type="button"] whose trimmed textContent === 'AI' inside the navbar (XPath //button[normalize-space()='AI'])

first_pass.fact: Label 'SAR', to '/object-detection', no testid, needs flag ObjectDetection, disabled offline.
Label 'History', to '/history', no testid (right group). Disabled offline and hidden when user.syncDisabled.

Label 'Settings', to '/settings', testid 'btn-settings' (right group). The user dropdown also has a Settings entry with testid drop-down-settings. The dropdown opens from the Avatar (data-testid user-menu, set on every Avatar) and holds the log-out entry data-testid log-out-btn.
Label 'Help', to '/help', no testid. It is in the right group and also in the mobile drawer.

The sync status icon has stable hooks: data-testid offline-status-indicator, or sync-status-indicator with data-state failed, syncing or synced. These are useful for waiting until the tablet is synced. The repo's own E2E NavbarPage uses btn-sites, btn-flights, btn-maps, btn-settings, btn-plane, btn-fleet, WingtraLogo and offline-status-indicator.

Nearly all modals use the in-house Dialog: Dialog.Container in 109 places, Dialog.Content in 125, Dialog.Header in 93. No material-tailwind Dialog or flowbite Modal is imported. Source never writes role="dialog" and has 0 aria-modal. The role comes from @floating-ui/react (^0.26.1) useRole(context) with its default role 'dialog', merged in through getFloatingProps and spread onto the panel div. That is library behaviour, so confirm it on device with a DOM read. The panel also gets aria-labelledby (set by Dialog.Header, a <div> with a useId id, not a heading) and aria-describedby (set by Dialog.Description). Its id is props.id, else the Container's id, else floating-ui's generated id. Only a few dialogs set a stable id, e.g. payload-internet-recovery, POLE_HEIGHT_MODAL_ID, TELEMETRY_RECONFIGURATION_MODAL_ID. The className is overwritten after the spread, so ConfirmDialog's className="Dialog" never reaches the DOM. The panel is portaled into #router-outlet inside FloatingOverlay with the attribute data-modal-overlay (z-[999]). Content is mounted only while the dialog is open, so the presence of the overlay or role means a dialog is open. Escape and an outside pointerdown close it unless dismissDisabled.
first_pass.selector: [data-modal-overlay] [role="dialog"] (last match = topmost); dialog by title: [role="dialog"] whose aria-labelledby target has the text

first_pass.fact: The X close button is a <div data-testid="btn-close-modal"> wrapper at the top right holding an IconButton <button>. That button has no testid, no aria-label and tabIndex -1, and is not rendered when hideClose is set. Dialog.Close is a separate Button with testid 'btn-close-modal', used in 4 files. It renders <button data-testid="btn-wrapper-btn-close-modal"> with an inner <span data-testid="btn-close-modal">. So [data-testid="btn-close-modal"] can match both the X wrapper div and a Dialog.Close span in the same dialog. The repo's E2E BasePage uses [data-testid="btn-close-modal"] and [data-modal-overlay].

AsyncModal (useAsyncModal) renders ConfirmDialog, built on Dialog.Container and Dialog.Content. Its Cancel Button has no testid, so it renders data-testid btn-wrapper-none. The action Button has testid 'btn-dialog-action' and fires on onMouseDown with preventDefault, not onClick. A real tap (adb) works, but JS element.click() does not trigger it; dispatch mousedown instead.
first_pass.selector: button[data-testid="btn-wrapper-btn-dialog-action"]; cancel: [role="dialog"] button with the cancel text

first_pass.fact: The Login screen (route /login) is a react-hook-form form with two FormTextFields, name="email" and name="password" (type="password"). Neither has a testId, and their DOM ids are unstable useId values. The password input switches to type="text" when the eye icon is tapped, so select it by name, not type. Labels and placeholders from en.json: 'Email' / 'e.g. wingtrauser@gmail.com' and 'Password' / 'Your password'. The Login button is the shared Button with type="submit", form={formId}, color orange, text t('actions.login') = 'Login', and no testid (so data-testid btn-wrapper-none). The page <h1> also reads 'Login', so matching on text is ambiguous; use the submit button. Other hooks: the forgot-password link is data-testid forgot-password-btn and the create-account link is create-new-account-btn. Wrong email or password shows a field error under the input, not a toast. A network failure shows a toast. The repo's E2E LoginPage uses exactly input[name="email"], input[name="password"] and button[type="submit"].

The app uses react-toastify 9.1.3 (^9.1.3, lockfile react-toastify@9.1.3). A single <ToastContainer> has position bottom-right, hideProgressBar, icon={false} and closeButton={false]. Its stylesheet is imported in index.tsx and the app overrides the standard classes in styles/toastr.css: .Toastify__toast-container, .Toastify__toast, .Toastify__toast-body, .Toastify__toast--default, --info, --success, --warning and --error. So the DOM uses the stock v9 class names: .Toastify__toast-container--bottom-right, .Toastify__toast plus .Toastify__toast--<type>, and .Toastify__toast-body (react-toastify gives the body role="alert" by default; library behaviour, not in this repo). The in-flight FlyToastr reuses the same container.

Each toast's content is ToastItem, a <div data-testid="notification-label"> holding a title Typography (default 'Unexpected error' when an error is passed) and a text Typography. Its close button is <button aria-label="Close" data-testid="notification-close">. Auto-close times: success 5000 ms, warning 10000 ms, neutral (type info) 5000 ms, error 10000 ms. FlyToastr's BlockingError never auto-closes. The repo's E2E waits for a toast with $('[data-testid="notification-label"]*=<text>').

'Report sent' appears in the Swiss Army Knife ReportingModal dialog in its 'done' state. It is Typography text inside <div data-testid="flight-success-modal-pop-up">, followed by Buttons 'Go to ticket' and 'Finish' (both untagged, data-testid btn-wrapper-none). The same testid is also used by the 'Reporting ...' in-progress state, so match on the text. While in progress, the close X is hidden and dismiss is disabled. ReportingModal's real toasts are: warning "Couldn't attach the flight plan link..."; error "Couldn't create report, retry or cancel."; errors 'ClickUp task not created yet.', 'Failed to auto attach log files.' and 'Failed to upload one or more files.'. The modal's Next button is an untagged type="submit" Button with the text 'Next'. The 'Attach more files in the next step' option is a FormToggleSwitch (role="checkbox"), which is why a substring match on 'Next' can hit it.
